name: Arkansas
sources: 2026 rates and brackets (top rate 3.7%; schedule for net income up to $94,700, schedule above it, bracket adjustment $94,701–$97,600): HB 1001, 2026 First Extraordinary Session, https://npr.brightspotcdn.com/a3/71/ed966e5b46c5be3992703b405077/binder1.pdf; summary https://tax.thomsonreuters.com/news/arkansas-cuts-individual-and-corporate-income-tax-rates/
2026 withholding formula top row starts at $97,601: https://news.bloombergtax.com/payroll/arkansas-reduces-highest-tax-rate-in-2026-withholding-methods

Standard deduction $2,470 ($4,940 joint), $29 personal credits (taxpayer, spouse, dependent, 65+, and 65 Special for those not claiming the retirement exemption): 2025 AR1000F instructions, https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025_AR1000F_and_AR1000NR_Instructions.pdf
50% of net long-term gain taxable: 2025 AR1000D, https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025_AR1000D_CapitalGains.pdf

Itemized deductions (medical over 10% of AGI, real estate and personal property taxes, mortgage interest, contributions): 2025 AR3, https://www.dfa.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025_AR3_ItemizedDeduction.pdf
provisional: Standard deduction $2,470 ($4,940 joint) is the 2025 amount; Arkansas indexes it and has not published 2026.
The $29 personal tax credits are the 2025 amount.
Bracket thresholds are the amounts written into HB 1001; the law indexes them yearly, so the 2026 tables could differ slightly (the 2026 withholding formula matches them).
notes: Couples who both have income can often pay less by filing separately on the same Arkansas return; this estimate uses joint filing.
Between $94,700 and $97,600 of taxable income Arkansas phases out its lower rates, shown here as a 13.6% bracket.
Arkansas's low-income tax tables are not included.
